import json
import os
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
import pytest

from negotiator.config import REPO_ROOT, Settings
from negotiator.data import WorldData

DATA = REPO_ROOT / "negotiation-arena-kit" / "data"
SIM_BIN = Path(sys.executable).parent / "arena-sim"


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def world() -> WorldData:
    return WorldData(DATA)


def _free_port() -> int:
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        return s.getsockname()[1]


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def sim(tmp_path_factory) -> Settings:
    """arena-sim from the starter kit on a free port, without the 60 s clock, and a simulator key."""
    port = _free_port()
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [str(SIM_BIN), "serve", "--port", str(port), "--no-clock", "--data", str(DATA)],
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    try:
        for _ in range(100):
            try:
                if httpx.get(f"{url}/health", timeout=1).status_code == 200:
                    break
            except httpx.HTTPError:
                time.sleep(0.1)
        else:
            pytest.skip("arena-sim did not start")
        key = httpx.post(
            f"{url}/v1/register",
            json={"team_name": "pytest", "event_code": "sim"},
            headers={"X-Move-Id": "pytest-register"},
        ).json()["api_key"]
        runs = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("runs")
        os.environ.pop("NEGOTIATOR_FINAL", None)
        yield Settings.from_env(arena_url=url, api_key=key, runs_dir=Path(runs))
    finally:
        proc.terminate()
        proc.wait(timeout=10)


def load(path: Path) -> dict:
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
"""The must-haves: guards that prevent a zero, the supplier profile, the concession logic, end to end."""

import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

from negotiator.chats import write_chats
from negotiator.client import ArenaClient
from negotiator.config import REPO_ROOT, Settings
from negotiator.data import WorldData
from negotiator.guards import accept_problems, clean_message, sheet_problems
from negotiator.lessons import write_lessons
from negotiator.profile import build_profile
from negotiator.report import write_report
from negotiator.runner import play_many
from negotiator.session import Negotiation, ThreadState
from negotiator.strategy import TacticalStrategy
from negotiator.strategy.tactical import POLICIES, parse_breakdown
from negotiator.telemetry import Recorder

SIM_CASES = REPO_ROOT / "negotiation-arena-kit" / "starter-kit" / "arena_kit" / "sim_cases"
QUOTE_TEXT = """Quotation
Offered terms
Unit price (EUR) 17.47
Our standard terms
Payment terms (days net) 30
Lead time (days) 70
Incoterm FCA
"""


def case(**buyer_overrides) -> dict:
    c = json.loads((SIM_CASES / "S01.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    c["buyer"].update(buyer_overrides)
    return c


def negotiation(tmp_path: Path, world: WorldData | None, c: dict, offer: dict, std_text: str = QUOTE_TEXT):
    neg = Negotiation(None, Recorder(tmp_path), world)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    neg.case, neg.case_id, neg.session_id = c, c["case_id"], "s1"
    sid = c["suppliers"][0]
    t = ThreadState(sid)
    t.messages.append(
        {
            "from": f"sales@{sid}",
            "status": "open",
            "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:x-0", "terms": offer}],
            "attachments": [{"name": "quote-0.pdf", "text": std_text}] if std_text else [],
        }
    )
    neg.threads[sid] = t
    return neg, sid


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- guards
def test_accept_guard_passes_a_good_sheet(tmp_path, world) -> None:
    neg, sid = negotiation(tmp_path, world, case(), {"unit_price": 16.0, "payment_days": 60})
    assert accept_problems(neg, sid, "offer:x-0") == []


def test_accept_guard_refuses_a_stale_sheet(tmp_path, world) -> None:
    neg, sid = negotiation(tmp_path, world, case(), {"unit_price": 16.0, "payment_days": 60})
    assert accept_problems(neg, sid, "offer:x-old")


def test_accept_guard_refuses_a_broken_must_have(tmp_path, world) -> None:
    c = case(must_haves=[{"field": "payment_days", "op": ">=", "value": 45}])
    neg, sid = negotiation(tmp_path, world, c, {"unit_price": 16.0, "payment_days": 30})
    assert any("must-have" in p for p in accept_problems(neg, sid, "offer:x-0"))


def test_accept_guard_reads_must_haves_on_the_standard_terms(tmp_path, world) -> None:
    """lead_time_days is not on the sheet and not fixed: it closes on the quote PDF's 70 days."""
    c = case(must_haves=[{"field": "lead_time_days", "op": "<=", "value": 50}])
    del c["fixed_terms"]["lead_time_days"]
    neg, sid = negotiation(tmp_path, world, c, {"unit_price": 16.0, "payment_days": 60})
    assert any("must-have" in p for p in accept_problems(neg, sid, "offer:x-0"))


def test_accept_guard_refuses_an_unknown_must_have_field(tmp_path, world) -> None:
"""Hard rules that keep a case from scoring 0 by mistake. Code, not judgement; checked before every
send and every accept, whatever the strategy decided.

Accept:  the sheet is the supplier's current standing offer; it keeps every must-have on the terms
         it would really close on (sheet, then the supplier's standard terms from its quote PDF) -
         and a must-have field we cannot read from either counts as broken; C is finite and beats
         the alternative - and, when there is one, the cheapest opening too (else the alternative
         scores at least as much).
Send:    every term sheet carries exactly the negotiable fields with allowed values and keeps the
         must-haves (a supplier may agree to any sheet we send, and we must be able to accept it);
         every cited ID exists in the data, the case's facts or this session's offers - a sentence
         whose IDs are all unknown goes, and so does a threat or an "other offer" without a rival's
         offer cited (conduct.py); at most 3 sheets and 20 refs.
"""

import math
import re

from arena_kit.cost import must_haves_ok

from negotiator.conduct import unsupported_sentences

ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):[\w.:@#/-]*\w")
MAX_SHEETS = 3
MAX_REFS = 20


def unreadable_must_have_fields(case: dict, terms: dict, standard: dict | None) -> list[str]:
    """Must-have fields neither the sheet, the supplier's standard terms nor the case fixes.

    `closing_terms` fills such gaps from the buyer's plan (e.g. lead time = what we need), which
    would let a sheet pass that the arena closes on the supplier's real standard - unknown to us."""
    known = {**(standard or {}), **case.get("fixed_terms", {}), **{k: v for k, v in terms.items() if v is not None}}
    return [m["field"] for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []) if m["field"] not in known]


def accept_problems(neg, supplier_id: str, term_sheet_id: str | None) -> list[str]:
    """Why accepting this sheet would be a mistake (empty: safe)."""
    t = neg.threads.get(supplier_id)
    if t is None:
        return ["unknown supplier"]
    standing_id, terms = t.standing
    problems = []
    if not term_sheet_id or term_sheet_id != standing_id:
        # the arena closes on the primary sheet whatever id we send (P10): only that one can be accepted
        problems.append(f"{term_sheet_id} is not the standing offer {standing_id}")
    if not terms or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
        problems.append("the standing offer has no price")
        return problems
    std = t.standard_terms
    if missing := unreadable_must_have_fields(neg.case, terms, std):
        problems.append(f"must-have field(s) {missing} unknown: no quote PDF standard terms")
    if not must_haves_ok(neg.case, terms, std):
        problems.append("breaks a must-have")
    c = neg.cost(supplier_id, terms)
    if not math.isfinite(c):
        problems.append("C is not finite")
    elif c >= neg.c_alt:
        problems.append(f"C {c:,.0f} does not beat the alternative {neg.c_alt:,.0f}")
    elif math.isfinite(neg.c_alt) and c >= neg.c_open:
        # a deal no better than the cheapest opening scores 0; the alternative scores at least that
        problems.append(f"C {c:,.0f} is not better than the opening {neg.c_open:,.0f}")
    return problems


def sheet_problems(case: dict, terms: dict) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    negotiable = case["negotiable"]
    if set(terms) != set(negotiable):
        problems.append(f"fields {sorted(terms)} != negotiable {sorted(negotiable)}")
    options = case.get("term_options", {})
    for f, v in terms.items():
        if f == "unit_price":
            if not isinstance(v, int | float) or v <= 0:
                problems.append(f"unit_price {v!r}")
        elif options.get(f) and v not in options[f]:
            problems.append(f"{f}={v!r} not in options")
    if not must_haves_ok(case, terms):
        problems.append("breaks a must-have")
    return problems


def known_id(neg, ref: str) -> bool:
    if neg.data and neg.data.fact(ref):
        return True
    if ref in (neg.case.get("facts") or {}):
        return True
    return any(
        s.get("term_sheet_id") == ref
        for t in neg.threads.values()
        for m in t.supplier_messages
        for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []
    )


def clean_message(neg, supplier_id: str, message: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    """The message with invalid sheets and unknown IDs removed, and what was removed."""
    removed: list[str] = []
    sheets = []
    for sheet in (message.get("term_sheets") or [])[:MAX_SHEETS]:
        problems = sheet_problems(neg.case, sheet.get("terms", {}))
        if problems:
            removed.append(f"sheet {sheet.get('terms')}: {'; '.join(problems)}")
        elif sheet not in sheets:
            sheets.append(sheet)
    refs = []
    for ref in message.get("refs") or []:
        if known_id(neg, ref):
            if ref not in refs:
                refs.append(ref)
        else:
            removed.append(f"ref {ref}")

    def keep(m: re.Match) -> str:
        if known_id(neg, m.group(0)):
            return m.group(0)
        removed.append(f"body id {m.group(0)}")
        return ""

    # conduct.py: no claim without its source, no threat or "other offer" we cannot show
    rival_ids = {
        s.get("term_sheet_id")
        for other, t in neg.threads.items()
        if other != supplier_id
        for m in t.supplier_messages
        for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []
    }
    rival_cited = any(r in rival_ids or r.startswith("quote:") for r in refs)
    body, unsupported = unsupported_sentences(
        message.get("body") or "", ID_RE, lambda i: known_id(neg, i), rival_cited
    )
    removed += [f"unsupported sentence: {s}" for s in unsupported]
    body = ID_RE.sub(keep, body)
    body = re.sub(r"\s*\(\s*[,;\s]*\)", "", body)
    out = {**message, "body": body[:8000], "subject": (message.get("subject") or "")[:300], "refs": refs[:MAX_REFS]}
    if "term_sheets" in message:
        out["term_sheets"] = sheets
    return out, removed
"""The strategy interface. The runner calls it; `Negotiation` holds the state it reads.

Per thread the runner asks `decide(neg, supplier_id)`:
  message    send this e-mail (subject, body, term sheets, refs)
  hold       this thread is settled for now (agreed, final offer, close enough, out of rounds)
  drop       this thread is over for us (walked away, no bid, hopeless)
  accept     close the case on this supplier's standing term sheet
  walk_away  close the case without a deal
When every thread is held or dropped, `conclude(neg)` makes the closing move (accept or walk away).
While other threads still negotiate, a held thread's 60 s clock keeps running: `keepalive` returns a
message that keeps it alive (or None to let it be).
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Literal, Protocol

from negotiator.session import Negotiation

Kind = Literal["message", "hold", "drop", "accept", "walk_away"]


@dataclass
class Decision:
    kind: Kind
    supplier_id: str | None = None
    message: dict | None = None
    term_sheet_id: str | None = None
    rationale: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    @classmethod
    def hold(cls, supplier_id: str, why: str, **extra) -> "Decision":
        return cls("hold", supplier_id, rationale={"why": why, **extra})

    @classmethod
    def drop(cls, supplier_id: str, why: str, **extra) -> "Decision":
        return cls("drop", supplier_id, rationale={"why": why, **extra})


class Strategy(Protocol):
    name: str

    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None: ...

    def decide(self, neg: Negotiation, supplier_id: str) -> Decision: ...

    def conclude(self, neg: Negotiation) -> Decision: ...

    def keepalive(self, neg: Negotiation, supplier_id: str) -> dict | None: ...

from negotiator.lessons import write_lessons

from negotiator.report import write_report
from negotiator.runner import play_many
from negotiator.session import Negotiation, ThreadState

from negotiator.telemetry import Recorder

SIM_CASES = REPO_ROOT / "negotiation-arena-kit" / "starter-kit" / "arena_kit" / "sim_cases"
QUOTE_TEXT = """Quotation
Offered terms
Unit price (EUR) 17.47
Our standard terms
Payment terms (days net) 30
Lead time (days) 70
Incoterm FCA
"""


def case(**buyer_overrides) -> dict:
    c = json.loads((SIM_CASES / "S01.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    c["buyer"].update(buyer_overrides)
    return c


def negotiation(tmp_path: Path, world: WorldData | None, c: dict, offer: dict, std_text: str = QUOTE_TEXT):
    neg = Negotiation(None, Recorder(tmp_path), world)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    neg.case, neg.case_id, neg.session_id = c, c["case_id"], "s1"
    sid = c["suppliers"][0]
    t = ThreadState(sid)
    t.messages.append(
        {
            "from": f"sales@{sid}",
            "status": "open",
            "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:x-0", "terms": offer}],
            "attachments": [{"name": "quote-0.pdf", "text": std_text}] if std_text else [],
        }
    )
    neg.threads[sid] = t
    return neg, sid


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- guards
def test_accept_guard_passes_a_good_sheet(tmp_path, world) -> None:
    neg, sid = negotiation(tmp_path, world, case(), {"unit_price": 16.0, "payment_days": 60})
    assert accept_problems(neg, sid, "offer:x-0") == []


def test_accept_guard_refuses_a_stale_sheet(tmp_path, world) -> None:
    neg, sid = negotiation(tmp_path, world, case(), {"unit_price": 16.0, "payment_days": 60})
    assert accept_problems(neg, sid, "offer:x-old")


def test_accept_guard_refuses_a_broken_must_have(tmp_path, world) -> None:
    c = case(must_haves=[{"field": "payment_days", "op": ">=", "value": 45}])
    neg, sid = negotiation(tmp_path, world, c, {"unit_price": 16.0, "payment_days": 30})
    assert any("must-have" in p for p in accept_problems(neg, sid, "offer:x-0"))


def test_accept_guard_reads_must_haves_on_the_standard_terms(tmp_path, world) -> None:
    """lead_time_days is not on the sheet and not fixed: it closes on the quote PDF's 70 days."""
    c = case(must_haves=[{"field": "lead_time_days", "op": "<=", "value": 50}])
    del c["fixed_terms"]["lead_time_days"]
    neg, sid = negotiation(tmp_path, world, c, {"unit_price": 16.0, "payment_days": 60})
    assert any("must-have" in p for p in accept_problems(neg, sid, "offer:x-0"))


def test_accept_guard_refuses_an_unknown_must_have_field(tmp_path, world) -> None:
"""Hard rules that keep a case from scoring 0 by mistake. Code, not judgement; checked before every
send and every accept, whatever the strategy decided.

Accept:  the sheet is the supplier's current standing offer; it keeps every must-have on the terms
         it would really close on (sheet, then the supplier's standard terms from its quote PDF) -
         and a must-have field we cannot read from either counts as broken; C is finite and beats
         the alternative - and, when there is one, the cheapest opening too (else the alternative
         scores at least as much).
Send:    every term sheet carries exactly the negotiable fields with allowed values and keeps the
         must-haves (a supplier may agree to any sheet we send, and we must be able to accept it);
         every cited ID exists in the data, the case's facts or this session's offers - a sentence
         whose IDs are all unknown goes, and so does a threat or an "other offer" without a rival's
         offer cited (conduct.py); at most 3 sheets and 20 refs.
"""

import math
import re

from arena_kit.cost import must_haves_ok

from negotiator.conduct import unsupported_sentences

ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):[\w.:@#/-]*\w")
MAX_SHEETS = 3
MAX_REFS = 20


def unreadable_must_have_fields(case: dict, terms: dict, standard: dict | None) -> list[str]:
    """Must-have fields neither the sheet, the supplier's standard terms nor the case fixes.

    `closing_terms` fills such gaps from the buyer's plan (e.g. lead time = what we need), which
    would let a sheet pass that the arena closes on the supplier's real standard - unknown to us."""
    known = {**(standard or {}), **case.get("fixed_terms", {}), **{k: v for k, v in terms.items() if v is not None}}
    return [m["field"] for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []) if m["field"] not in known]


def accept_problems(neg, supplier_id: str, term_sheet_id: str | None) -> list[str]:
    """Why accepting this sheet would be a mistake (empty: safe)."""
    t = neg.threads.get(supplier_id)
    if t is None:
        return ["unknown supplier"]
    standing_id, terms = t.standing
    problems = []
    if not term_sheet_id or term_sheet_id != standing_id:
        # the arena closes on the primary sheet whatever id we send (P10): only that one can be accepted
        problems.append(f"{term_sheet_id} is not the standing offer {standing_id}")
    if not terms or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
        problems.append("the standing offer has no price")
        return problems
    std = t.standard_terms
    if missing := unreadable_must_have_fields(neg.case, terms, std):
        problems.append(f"must-have field(s) {missing} unknown: no quote PDF standard terms")
    if not must_haves_ok(neg.case, terms, std):
        problems.append("breaks a must-have")
    c = neg.cost(supplier_id, terms)
    if not math.isfinite(c):
        problems.append("C is not finite")
    elif c >= neg.c_alt:
        problems.append(f"C {c:,.0f} does not beat the alternative {neg.c_alt:,.0f}")
    elif math.isfinite(neg.c_alt) and c >= neg.c_open:
        # a deal no better than the cheapest opening scores 0; the alternative scores at least that
        problems.append(f"C {c:,.0f} is not better than the opening {neg.c_open:,.0f}")
    return problems


def sheet_problems(case: dict, terms: dict) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    negotiable = case["negotiable"]
    if set(terms) != set(negotiable):
        problems.append(f"fields {sorted(terms)} != negotiable {sorted(negotiable)}")
    options = case.get("term_options", {})
    for f, v in terms.items():
        if f == "unit_price":
            if not isinstance(v, int | float) or v <= 0:
                problems.append(f"unit_price {v!r}")
        elif options.get(f) and v not in options[f]:
            problems.append(f"{f}={v!r} not in options")
    if not must_haves_ok(case, terms):
        problems.append("breaks a must-have")
    return problems


def known_id(neg, ref: str) -> bool:
    if neg.data and neg.data.fact(ref):
        return True
    if ref in (neg.case.get("facts") or {}):
        return True
    return any(
        s.get("term_sheet_id") == ref
        for t in neg.threads.values()
        for m in t.supplier_messages
        for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []
    )


def clean_message(neg, supplier_id: str, message: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    """The message with invalid sheets and unknown IDs removed, and what was removed."""
    removed: list[str] = []
    sheets = []
    for sheet in (message.get("term_sheets") or [])[:MAX_SHEETS]:
        problems = sheet_problems(neg.case, sheet.get("terms", {}))
        if problems:
            removed.append(f"sheet {sheet.get('terms')}: {'; '.join(problems)}")
        elif sheet not in sheets:
            sheets.append(sheet)
    refs = []
    for ref in message.get("refs") or []:
        if known_id(neg, ref):
            if ref not in refs:
                refs.append(ref)
        else:
            removed.append(f"ref {ref}")

    def keep(m: re.Match) -> str:
        if known_id(neg, m.group(0)):
            return m.group(0)
        removed.append(f"body id {m.group(0)}")
        return ""

    # conduct.py: no claim without its source, no threat or "other offer" we cannot show
    rival_ids = {
        s.get("term_sheet_id")
        for other, t in neg.threads.items()
        if other != supplier_id
        for m in t.supplier_messages
        for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []
    }
    rival_cited = any(r in rival_ids or r.startswith("quote:") for r in refs)
    body, unsupported = unsupported_sentences(
        message.get("body") or "", ID_RE, lambda i: known_id(neg, i), rival_cited
    )
    removed += [f"unsupported sentence: {s}" for s in unsupported]
    body = ID_RE.sub(keep, body)
    body = re.sub(r"\s*\(\s*[,;\s]*\)", "", body)
    out = {**message, "body": body[:8000], "subject": (message.get("subject") or "")[:300], "refs": refs[:MAX_REFS]}
    if "term_sheets" in message:
        out["term_sheets"] = sheets
    return out, removed
"""The strategy interface. The runner calls it; `Negotiation` holds the state it reads.

Per thread the runner asks `decide(neg, supplier_id)`:
  message    send this e-mail (subject, body, term sheets, refs)
  hold       this thread is settled for now (agreed, final offer, close enough, out of rounds)
  drop       this thread is over for us (walked away, no bid, hopeless)
  accept     close the case on this supplier's standing term sheet
  walk_away  close the case without a deal
When every thread is held or dropped, `conclude(neg)` makes the closing move (accept or walk away).
While other threads still negotiate, a held thread's 60 s clock keeps running: `keepalive` returns a
message that keeps it alive (or None to let it be).
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Literal, Protocol

from negotiator.session import Negotiation

Kind = Literal["message", "hold", "drop", "accept", "walk_away"]


@dataclass
class Decision:
    kind: Kind
    supplier_id: str | None = None
    message: dict | None = None
    term_sheet_id: str | None = None
    rationale: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    @classmethod
    def hold(cls, supplier_id: str, why: str, **extra) -> "Decision":
        return cls("hold", supplier_id, rationale={"why": why, **extra})

    @classmethod
    def drop(cls, supplier_id: str, why: str, **extra) -> "Decision":
        return cls("drop", supplier_id, rationale={"why": why, **extra})


class Strategy(Protocol):
    name: str

    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None: ...

    def decide(self, neg: Negotiation, supplier_id: str) -> Decision: ...

    def conclude(self, neg: Negotiation) -> Decision: ...

    def keepalive(self, neg: Negotiation, supplier_id: str) -> dict | None: ...

"""Tactical buyer: category goal + supplier profile -> tactics; tit-for-tat Boulware concessions in C.

Ideas taken from ASTRA (Kwon et al., github.com/DSincerity/ASTRA-NegoAgent) - the tactics, not the
code: a model of the opponent, an optimiser over the published cost function, several offers of
equal value to us that differ in what they give the supplier, and concessions that answer the
supplier's (no move from it, no move from us).

Per case (prepare):
  - the category goal sets the policy: how deep we anchor, how slowly we concede (Boulware beta),
    how much of the supplier's move we answer (reciprocity), whether we protect its margin;
  - the supplier's profile (profile.py) adjusts it: idle capacity -> anchor deeper; fully booked or
    below cost -> shallower; cash-short -> offer early payment; hedged -> skip index arguments ...;
  - target C: the deepest credible price (anchor, should-cost, history, alternative), never below
    what the supplier can sell at (its full cost, plus the sustainable margin where squeezing costs C).

Per round (decide), all in C (our total cost, the score's currency):
  - their concession = drop of C of their standing sheet; ours = drop of the C we ask for;
  - next ask: the Boulware curve over the rounds we can still play (round limit and the clock),
    capped by reciprocity - if they did not move, we hold (then a half step to break a deadlock;
    the third stall settles the thread);
  - up to three term sheets at that same C: our C-optimal terms; a trade the supplier values
    (early payment for the cash-short, a long commitment for those who want volume or security);
    a pure price move on its own terms. Whatever it agrees to costs us the same.
  - arguments: checkable evidence picked by the profile; what came back irrelevant or contradicted
    is not used again.
Closing: the cheapest standing sheet that passes the guards (guards.py), else walk away; a
`final_offer` is probed once with a trade when walking would cost us little.
Conduct (conduct.py): honest, sourced, no empty threats, the supplier's margin respected - code-checked on send.
"""

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from arena_kit.cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, complete_offer

from negotiator.belief import FloorBelief
from negotiator.data import Evidence, WorldData
from negotiator.groundtruth import GroundTruth, estimate
from negotiator.guards import accept_problems
from negotiator.ledger import CITED_DRIVER, data_facts, reply_facts
from negotiator.menu import acceptance, priced_menu, proposed_values, requests_in, satisfies, structure_key
from negotiator.profile import SupplierProfile, build_profile
from negotiator.session import Negotiation
from negotiator.strategy.base import Decision
from negotiator.strategy.baseline import SIGNATURE, BaselineStrategy, describe
from negotiator.telemetry import log


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    anchor: float  # first ask: this share below the reference price
    beta: float  # Boulware exponent: > 1 concedes late
    reciprocity: float  # share of the supplier's last concession (in C) we answer at most
    markup: float  # floor vs the supplier's full cost when its margin does not cost us C (suppliers have
    # sold below full cost to keep volume: a leverage floor may sit a little under it)
    claims_first: int = 3  # arguments in the first e-mail
    trade_first: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # levers to offer the supplier, in order


POLICIES = {
    "leverage": Policy(anchor=0.10, beta=3.0, reciprocity=0.6, markup=-0.03),
    "routine": Policy(anchor=0.07, beta=2.0, reciprocity=0.8, markup=0.0),
    "quality_first": Policy(anchor=0.05, beta=2.5, reciprocity=0.8, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months",)),
    "stabilise": Policy(
        anchor=0.04, beta=2.0, reciprocity=1.0, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months", "volume_per_year")
    ),
    "secure_supply": Policy(
        anchor=0.03, beta=1.8, reciprocity=1.0, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months", "volume_per_year")
    ),
}
DEFAULT_POLICY = POLICIES["routine"]
STALL_EPS = 0.0005  # a C move below 0.05 % is no move
DONE_EPS = 0.001  # our ask within 0.1 % of their C: nothing left worth a round
ANCHOR_WITH_LEVERS = 0.25  # first ask 25 % under the quote where competition, material or capacity give a lever
ANCHOR_DATA_EXTRA = 0.05  # how much deeper the data may take the first ask
RELATIONSHIP_COST_FLOOR = 0.95  # never ask a strategic supplier below 95 % of its should-cost
ANCHOR_RELATIONSHIP = 0.04  # stabilise / secure_supply: below its margin the deal costs us
ANCHOR_PRICE_ONLY = 0.10  # ... and 10 % where only the price of a running relationship is at stake
MAX_ANCHOR = 0.15  # (kept for the experiments that import it)
MAX_ANCHOR_LEVERAGE = 0.18  # ... 18 % in leverage: floors sat 19-31 % under (D02, P05, P18), but a deeper first
# ask lost credibility (P05: Hrvelec walked after four rounds at 24-25 against its 34)
# without a cost estimate, anchor this far under the reference price (baseline v2's sandbox-tested depths)
GUESS_ANCHOR = {"leverage": 0.18, "routine": 0.12, "quality_first": 0.10, "stabilise": 0.06, "secure_supply": 0.05}
UNDER_FLOOR = 0.02  # the first ask sits this far under the supplier's estimated floor
# what a supplier's e-mail says between the lines (the replay of case:D01/D02 showed both kinds)
ROOM_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"can move further|come back to you on price|free capacity|step from your side|bridge the (?:remaining )?gap"
    r"|clarify this internally|happy to discuss|open to|we could consider|room to",
    re.I,
)
FIRM_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"cannot (?:reduce|lower|go) (?:the price )?(?:any )?further|all possible concessions"
    r"|no further (?:room|concession)|our (?:absolute )?limit|not able to move|this is our last"
    r"|must (?:\w+ )?(?:hold|maintain) our (?:current )?offer|does not allow us to reduce|unable to (?:reduce|improve)"
    r"|we maintain our (?:current )?offer",
    re.I,
)
APPROVAL_PENDING = re.compile(
    r"clarify (?:this |it )?internally|come back to you on (?:the )?price|my band|approv(?:e|al) (?:a|for) further|"
    r"check (?:the rest|internally)|discuss (?:this )?internally",
    re.I,
)
REANCHOR = 0.10  # an ungrounded floor the supplier undercuts at once: ask again this far under its price
BIG_STEP = 0.04  # a supplier move of 4 %+ in one round says it had room
UPPER_ROOM = 0.06  # the upper bound sits at least this far above our first ask
STOP_MARGIN = 0.01  # we take an offer within 1 % of where we expect the supplier to stop
MIN_STEP = 0.004  # every message moves at least 0.4 % of C: these bots punish a repeated offer
MAX_SPREAD = 0.08  # options of one message stay within 8 % of each other's price


def reply_signals(body: str) -> dict:
    """Room or firmness in the supplier's own words - a `final_offer` that asks for our step is no last word."""
    return {"room": bool(ROOM_SIGNALS.search(body or "")), "firm": bool(FIRM_SIGNALS.search(body or ""))}


EVIDENCE_FIRST = {  # profile trait / goal -> evidence kinds to put first
    "not_tracking_costs": ["index"],
    "open_book": ["should_cost"],
    "quality_first": ["quality", "scorecard"],
}


@dataclass
class Plan:
    supplier_id: str
    name: str
    policy: Policy
    profile: SupplierProfile
    open_c: float
    target_c: float
    floor_price: float | None
    full_cost: float | None
    gt: GroundTruth | None = None
    belief: FloorBelief | None = None  # where this supplier will stop with us - recomputed after every reply
    lower_c: float = -math.inf  # C at the supplier's estimated floor: take it at once
    upper_c: float = math.inf  # the most we accept when the deal is at risk - never said, never asked for
    evidence: list[Evidence] = field(default_factory=list)
    banned_kinds: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    our_c: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)  # the C we asked for, per round
    last_claims: list[Evidence] = field(default_factory=list)
    seen_replies: int = 0
    stalls: int = 0
    probed_final: bool = False
    price_matched: bool = False
    requests: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)  # levers the supplier asked for in its e-mails
    last_keys: frozenset = frozenset()  # the structures and prices we sent last
    offered: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # structure -> the highest price we offered for it
    volume_proved: bool = False
    proposed: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # field -> values the supplier put on its own sheets
    text_price: float | None = None  # a lower price it wrote in the text but not on a sheet
    text_price_used: bool = False
    alternatives_taken: set = field(default_factory=set)
    counters: list = field(default_factory=list)  # facts from its own e-mails that answer it - spent first
    used_sentences: set = field(default_factory=set)
    lever_turn: bool = False  # this round our step goes into a structure we have not offered yet
    pressures: list = field(default_factory=list)  # cost drivers it says weigh on it
    request_counts: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # lever -> replies that asked for it
    reanchored: bool = False
    asked_breakdown: bool = False
    breakdown_read: bool = False


# Candidate changes from the reviews, each switchable so it can be measured on its own (simulator with
# --jitter --strangers, then the sandbox) before it is adopted. Off by default.
FLAGS = {
    "strict_final": "a final offer: only its cheaper alternative, accept, or the RFQ probe - no written-price ask",
    "belief_cap": "the belief's extrapolation: step ratio capped at 0.6, never under 90 % of its lowest offer value",
    "probe_leader": "RFQ probe only when our ask is below the best offer on the table",
    "anchor_cap25": "first ask at most 25 % under the quote in total (base depth plus the data's extra)",
    "dedupe_series": "one argument per index series and case",
    "big_steps": "from round 2 our step is 2-4 % of C_open (at most 60 % of the gap)",
}


class TacticalStrategy(BaselineStrategy):
    name = "tactical"

    def __init__(self, data: WorldData | None = None, llm=None, **flags) -> None:
        super().__init__(data, llm)
        unknown = set(flags) - set(FLAGS)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown tactical flags: {sorted(unknown)}")
        self.flags = {name: bool(flags.get(name, False)) for name in FLAGS}
        self.used_series: set[str] = set()
        self.tplans: dict[str, Plan] = {}
        self.banned_case_kinds: set[str] = set()  # contradicted: never again in this case

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ prepare
    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None:
        buyer = neg.buyer
        goal = buyer.get("category_goal", "routine")
        parts = neg.case.get("parts", [])
        current = buyer.get("current_unit_price")
        for sid, thread in neg.threads.items():
            _, terms = thread.standing
            profile = build_profile(self.data, sid, neg.case)
            policy = self._policy(goal, profile)
            full_cost = self._full_cost(parts, sid)
            self._estimate_supplier(neg, sid, full_cost, profile)
            floor = self._floor(neg, full_cost, policy)
            open_c = neg.cost(sid, terms)
            gt = estimate(self.data, neg.case, sid, terms.get("unit_price"), tuple(profile.traits))
            if gt.lower and goal not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
                floor = gt.lower  # one floor: the ground truth's (it knows below-cost sellers and countries)
            target_c = self._target_c(neg, sid, terms, policy, profile, floor, current, gt)
            plan = Plan(sid, self._name(sid), policy, profile, open_c, target_c, floor, full_cost, gt)
            plan.lower_c, plan.upper_c = self._bounds_c(neg, sid, terms, gt, target_c, open_c)
            if terms.get("unit_price") is not None:
                rate = buyer.get("interest_rate", 0.08) * (2 if profile.has("cash_short") else 1)
                plan.belief = FloorBelief(neg.case, terms, thread.standard_terms, gt.lower, rate)
                plan.belief.capped = self.flags["belief_cap"]
                plan.belief.ppm = profile.ppm  # scorecard ppm: what a chargeback really costs it
            plan.evidence = self._evidence(neg, sid, terms.get("unit_price"), current) if terms else []
            if profile.has("hedged"):
                plan.banned_kinds.add("index")  # "not our reality" until its hedge runs out
            if gt.market_supports_ask:
                plan.banned_kinds.add("index")  # the indices back its ask: citing them helps it, not us
            self.tplans[sid] = plan
            neg.recorder.event(
                "plan",
                session_id=neg.session_id,
                case_id=neg.case_id,
                supplier_id=sid,
                strategy=self.name,
                goal=goal,
                policy=policy.__dict__,
                profile=profile.summary(),
                trait_refs=profile.traits,
                open_price=terms.get("unit_price"),
                open_c=open_c,
                target_c=target_c,
                lower_c=plan.lower_c,
                upper_c=plan.upper_c,
                ground_truth=gt.summary(),
                c_alt=neg.c_alt,
                floor_price=floor,
                full_cost=full_cost,
                evidence=[{"kind": e.kind, "refs": e.refs, "sentence": e.sentence} for e in plan.evidence],
            )
            log.info(
                "%s plan [%s %s]: price open %s lower %s upper %s (asked %s%%, justified %s%%) | C target %s upper %s",
                sid,
                goal,
                ",".join(sorted(profile.traits)) or "-",
                terms.get("unit_price"),
                gt.lower,
                gt.upper,
                gt.asked_pct,
                gt.justified_pct,
                _k(target_c),
                _k(plan.upper_c),
            )

    def _policy(self, goal: str, p: SupplierProfile) -> Policy:
        base = POLICIES.get(goal, DEFAULT_POLICY)
        anchor, beta, recip = base.anchor, base.beta, base.reciprocity
        trade = list(base.trade_first)
        if p.has("underutilised"):
            anchor, beta = anchor + 0.03, beta + 0.5
        markup = base.markup
        if p.has("full_order_book") or p.has("below_cost"):
            anchor = max(0.02, anchor - 0.03)
            markup = max(markup, 0.0)  # no room under its cost: it is already there or does not need us
        if p.has("price_frozen"):
            anchor = max(0.02, anchor - 0.02)
        if p.has("approval_ladder"):
            beta += 0.5  # it moves in small approved steps: no reason for us to move fast
        if p.has("cash_short"):
            trade.insert(0, "payment_days")
        if p.has("wants_volume") or p.has("full_order_book") or p.has("price_frozen"):
            trade += ["contract_months", "volume_per_year"]
        if p.has("we_pay_late") or p.has("relationship"):
            recip = min(1.0, recip + 0.1)
        return Policy(anchor, beta, recip, markup, base.claims_first, tuple(dict.fromkeys(trade)))

    def _evidence(self, neg, sid, open_price, current):
        out = super()._evidence(neg, sid, open_price, current)
        if self.data:
            out += self.data.evidence_orders(neg.case.get("parts", []), sid, open_price)
            out += data_facts(self.data, neg.case.get("parts", []))
        return sorted(out, key=lambda e: -e.strength)

    def _full_cost(self, parts: list[str], supplier_id: str) -> float | None:
        """The should-cost of THIS supplier's plant for a single-part case; None otherwise.

        Another supplier's estimate is a different plant (cost base, process) and a bundle's price is
        not one part's cost: guessing would push the floor and the margin charge the wrong way."""
        if not self.data or len(parts) != 1:
            return None
        rows = self.data.query(
            "SELECT unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ? AND supplier_id = ? ORDER BY estimate_date DESC",
            (parts[0], supplier_id),
        )
        return rows[0]["unit_cost"] if rows and rows[0]["unit_cost"] else None

    def _estimate_supplier(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, full_cost: float | None, p: SupplierProfile) -> None:
        """Our estimate of the supplier for the relationship term in C (stabilise, secure_supply)."""
        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not full_cost:
            neg.supplier_estimates.pop(sid, None)
            return
        std = neg.threads[sid].standard_terms
        if not {"payment_days", "incoterm"} <= std.keys():
            # no estimate without its standard terms: filling them in made the charge dominate every move (P01/P02
            # stopped negotiating in a dry run) - the shallow strategic anchor guards against the squeeze instead
            return
        rate = neg.buyer.get("interest_rate", 0.08)
        neg.supplier_estimates[sid] = {
            "full_cost": full_cost,
            "interest_rate": rate * 2 if p.has("cash_short") else rate,  # money now is dearer to it
            "usual_rate": rate,
            "standard": std,
        }

    def _update_upper(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, plan: Plan) -> None:
        """The upper bound follows the evidence: where this supplier will stop with us (its offers, last words,
        the shrinking path of its steps), priced on the best structure. Offline on 28 practice sessions this
        estimate met the real stopping point within 8 % before the first reply and 1-3 % by round 3-4.
        The anchor stays where the data put it; only how far we go and when we take it follow the supplier."""
        _, theirs = neg.threads[sid].standing
        insisted = {r for r, n in plan.request_counts.items() if n >= 2}
        stop_c, stop_terms = plan.belief.best_package(
            lambda t: neg.cost(sid, t),
            lambda t: neg.keeps_must_haves(sid, t),
            allow=lambda t: all(satisfies(neg.case, t, theirs or {}, r, plan.proposed) for r in insisted),
        )
        if not math.isfinite(stop_c):
            return
        _, terms = neg.threads[sid].standing
        cap = min(neg.c_alt, neg.cost(sid, terms) if terms else math.inf, plan.open_c)
        before = plan.upper_c
        plan.upper_c = min(max(stop_c * (1 + STOP_MARGIN), plan.target_c * (1 + UPPER_ROOM)), cap)
        neg.recorder.event(
            "belief",
            session_id=neg.session_id,
            supplier_id=sid,
            belief=plan.belief.summary(),
            stop_c=round(stop_c, 2),
            stop_price=(stop_terms or {}).get("unit_price"),
            upper_before=round(before, 2) if math.isfinite(before) else None,
            upper_after=round(plan.upper_c, 2) if math.isfinite(plan.upper_c) else None,
        )
        log.info(
            "%s belief: stop ~%s (price %s), upper %s -> %s",
            sid,
            _k(stop_c),
            (stop_terms or {}).get("unit_price"),
            _k(before),
            _k(plan.upper_c),
        )

    def _floor(self, neg: Negotiation, full_cost: float | None, policy: Policy) -> float | None:
        if not full_cost:
            return None
        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            margin = neg.buyer.get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
            return round(full_cost / (1 - margin / 100), 2)
        return round(full_cost * (1 + policy.markup), 2)

    def _target_c(self, neg, sid, terms, policy, profile, floor, current, gt: GroundTruth | None = None) -> float:
        """The C of our first ask: the deepest credible price on our C-optimal terms - just under the
        supplier's estimated floor when we have one, else an anchor below the reference price."""
        open_price = terms.get("unit_price")
        if open_price is None:
            return math.inf
        price_only = bool(gt and gt.lower and gt.lower >= open_price * 0.95)  # the prior says: only the price moves
        depth = ANCHOR_PRICE_ONLY if price_only else ANCHOR_WITH_LEVERS
        extra = ANCHOR_DATA_EXTRA
        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            depth, extra = min(depth, ANCHOR_RELATIONSHIP), 0.0  # squeezing a strategic supplier costs us C
        # round 1 carries 67 % of all supplier movement and no supplier ever walked over a deep first offer
        # (0 of 917 replies); within a case deeper first offers went with better scores - so we open deep
        candidates = [open_price * (1 - depth)]
        if gt and gt.lower and gt.grounded:
            candidates.append(gt.lower * (1 - UNDER_FLOOR))
        alt_price = ((neg.buyer.get("alternative") or {}).get("terms") or {}).get("unit_price")
        if alt_price and alt_price < open_price:
            candidates.append(alt_price * 0.98)
        # the data may take it deeper - a cheaper alternative, a low grounded floor - but not past 5 points more
        if self.flags["anchor_cap25"]:
            extra = max(0.0, min(extra, 0.25 - depth))
        price = max(min(candidates), open_price * (1 - depth - extra))
        # no hard floor for strategic suppliers: the relationship term already prices a squeeze in C, and
        # our cost estimate can sit above its real one (P02: should-cost 380 over a 371 quote, C_best ~364)
        price = min(price, open_price)
        ideal = complete_offer(neg.case, self._optimise(neg, sid, {**terms, "unit_price": round(price, 2)}))
        return min(neg.cost(sid, ideal), neg.cost(sid, terms))

    def _bounds_c(self, neg, sid, terms, gt: GroundTruth, target_c: float, open_c: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """The bounds in C, on our C-optimal terms: a fair price on poor terms (a short contract that
        leaves need uncovered, early payment, dear freight) must not pass as a good deal."""
        lower_c, upper_c = -math.inf, min(open_c, neg.c_alt)
        if gt.lower:
            lower_c = neg.cost(sid, self._ideal(neg, sid, terms, gt.lower))
        if gt.upper:
            upper_c = min(upper_c, neg.cost(sid, self._ideal(neg, sid, terms, gt.upper)))
        # room to concede above our first ask, whatever the calibration says (P05: an 18 % anchor over a 22 %
        # floor left upper == anchor and only 0.4 % steps) - never above its quote or our alternative
        return lower_c, min(max(upper_c, target_c * (1 + UPPER_ROOM)), open_c, neg.c_alt)

    def _ideal(self, neg, sid, terms: dict, price: float) -> dict:
        return complete_offer(neg.case, self._optimise(neg, sid, {**terms, "unit_price": round(price, 2)}))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ per thread
    def decide(self, neg: Negotiation, supplier_id: str) -> Decision:
        t, plan = neg.threads[supplier_id], self.tplans[supplier_id]
        if not t.live:
            return Decision.drop(supplier_id, f"thread {t.status}")
        self._learn(neg, supplier_id, plan)
        sheet_id, theirs = neg.best_offer(supplier_id)  # judge it by its best sheet for us, not its first
        if theirs.get("unit_price") is None or not math.isfinite(plan.target_c):
            return Decision.hold(supplier_id, "no price to negotiate on")
        early_signals = reply_signals(t.latest.get("body", ""))
        last_word_now = t.status == "final_offer" or (early_signals["firm"] and t.rounds_used > 0)
        if not (self.flags["strict_final"] and last_word_now):
            if text := self._text_price_offer(neg, supplier_id, plan):
                return text  # it wrote a lower price than it sheeted: ask for that first
        if t.status == "agreed":
            if take := self._take_agreed(neg, supplier_id):
                return take

"""Tactical buyer: category goal + supplier profile -> tactics; tit-for-tat Boulware concessions in C.

Ideas taken from ASTRA (Kwon et al., github.com/DSincerity/ASTRA-NegoAgent) - the tactics, not the
code: a model of the opponent, an optimiser over the published cost function, several offers of
equal value to us that differ in what they give the supplier, and concessions that answer the
supplier's (no move from it, no move from us).

Per case (prepare):
  - the category goal sets the policy: how deep we anchor, how slowly we concede (Boulware beta),
    how much of the supplier's move we answer (reciprocity), whether we protect its margin;
  - the supplier's profile (profile.py) adjusts it: idle capacity -> anchor deeper; fully booked or
    below cost -> shallower; cash-short -> offer early payment; hedged -> skip index arguments ...;
  - target C: the deepest credible price (anchor, should-cost, history, alternative), never below
    what the supplier can sell at (its full cost, plus the sustainable margin where squeezing costs C).

Per round (decide), all in C (our total cost, the score's currency):
  - their concession = drop of C of their standing sheet; ours = drop of the C we ask for;
  - next ask: the Boulware curve over the rounds we can still play (round limit and the clock),
    capped by reciprocity - if they did not move, we hold (then a half step to break a deadlock;
    the third stall settles the thread);
  - up to three term sheets at that same C: our C-optimal terms; a trade the supplier values
    (early payment for the cash-short, a long commitment for those who want volume or security);
    a pure price move on its own terms. Whatever it agrees to costs us the same.
  - arguments: checkable evidence picked by the profile; what came back irrelevant or contradicted
    is not used again.
Closing: the cheapest standing sheet that passes the guards (guards.py), else walk away; a
`final_offer` is probed once with a trade when walking would cost us little.
Conduct (conduct.py): honest, sourced, no empty threats, the supplier's margin respected - code-checked on send.
"""

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from arena_kit.cost import RELATIONSHIP_GOALS, complete_offer

from negotiator.belief import FloorBelief
from negotiator.data import Evidence, WorldData
from negotiator.groundtruth import GroundTruth, estimate
from negotiator.guards import accept_problems
from negotiator.ledger import CITED_DRIVER, data_facts, reply_facts
from negotiator.menu import acceptance, priced_menu, proposed_values, requests_in, satisfies, structure_key
from negotiator.profile import SupplierProfile, build_profile
from negotiator.session import Negotiation
from negotiator.strategy.base import Decision
from negotiator.strategy.baseline import SIGNATURE, BaselineStrategy, describe
from negotiator.telemetry import log


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    anchor: float  # first ask: this share below the reference price
    beta: float  # Boulware exponent: > 1 concedes late
    reciprocity: float  # share of the supplier's last concession (in C) we answer at most
    markup: float  # floor vs the supplier's full cost when its margin does not cost us C (suppliers have
    # sold below full cost to keep volume: a leverage floor may sit a little under it)
    claims_first: int = 3  # arguments in the first e-mail
    trade_first: tuple[str, ...] = ()  # levers to offer the supplier, in order


POLICIES = {
    "leverage": Policy(anchor=0.10, beta=3.0, reciprocity=0.6, markup=-0.03),
    "routine": Policy(anchor=0.07, beta=2.0, reciprocity=0.8, markup=0.0),
    "quality_first": Policy(anchor=0.05, beta=2.5, reciprocity=0.8, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months",)),
    "stabilise": Policy(
        anchor=0.04, beta=2.0, reciprocity=1.0, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months", "volume_per_year")
    ),
    "secure_supply": Policy(
        anchor=0.03, beta=1.8, reciprocity=1.0, markup=0.0, trade_first=("contract_months", "volume_per_year")
    ),
}
DEFAULT_POLICY = POLICIES["routine"]
STALL_EPS = 0.0005  # a C move below 0.05 % is no move
DONE_EPS = 0.001  # our ask within 0.1 % of their C: nothing left worth a round
ANCHOR_WITH_LEVERS = 0.25  # first ask 25 % under the quote where competition, material or capacity give a lever
ANCHOR_DATA_EXTRA = 0.05  # how much deeper the data may take the first ask
RELATIONSHIP_COST_FLOOR = 0.95  # never ask a strategic supplier below 95 % of its should-cost
ANCHOR_RELATIONSHIP = 0.04  # stabilise / secure_supply: below its margin the deal costs us
ANCHOR_PRICE_ONLY = 0.10  # ... and 10 % where only the price of a running relationship is at stake
MAX_ANCHOR = 0.15  # (kept for the experiments that import it)
MAX_ANCHOR_LEVERAGE = 0.18  # ... 18 % in leverage: floors sat 19-31 % under (D02, P05, P18), but a deeper first
# ask lost credibility (P05: Hrvelec walked after four rounds at 24-25 against its 34)
# without a cost estimate, anchor this far under the reference price (baseline v2's sandbox-tested depths)
GUESS_ANCHOR = {"leverage": 0.18, "routine": 0.12, "quality_first": 0.10, "stabilise": 0.06, "secure_supply": 0.05}
UNDER_FLOOR = 0.02  # the first ask sits this far under the supplier's estimated floor
# what a supplier's e-mail says between the lines (the replay of case:D01/D02 showed both kinds)
ROOM_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"can move further|come back to you on price|free capacity|step from your side|bridge the (?:remaining )?gap"
    r"|clarify this internally|happy to discuss|open to|we could consider|room to",
    re.I,
)
FIRM_SIGNALS = re.compile(
    r"cannot (?:reduce|lower|go) (?:the price )?(?:any )?further|all possible concessions"
    r"|no further (?:room|concession)|our (?:absolute )?limit|not able to move|this is our last"
    r"|must (?:\w+ )?(?:hold|maintain) our (?:current )?offer|does not allow us to reduce|unable to (?:reduce|improve)"
    r"|we maintain our (?:current )?offer",
    re.I,
)
APPROVAL_PENDING = re.compile(
    r"clarify (?:this |it )?internally|come back to you on (?:the )?price|my band|approv(?:e|al) (?:a|for) further|"
    r"check (?:the rest|internally)|discuss (?:this )?internally",
    re.I,
)
REANCHOR = 0.10  # an ungrounded floor the supplier undercuts at once: ask again this far under its price
BIG_STEP = 0.04  # a supplier move of 4 %+ in one round says it had room
UPPER_ROOM = 0.06  # the upper bound sits at least this far above our first ask
STOP_MARGIN = 0.01  # we take an offer within 1 % of where we expect the supplier to stop
MIN_STEP = 0.004  # every message moves at least 0.4 % of C: these bots punish a repeated offer
MAX_SPREAD = 0.08  # options of one message stay within 8 % of each other's price


def reply_signals(body: str) -> dict:
    """Room or firmness in the supplier's own words - a `final_offer` that asks for our step is no last word."""
    return {"room": bool(ROOM_SIGNALS.search(body or "")), "firm": bool(FIRM_SIGNALS.search(body or ""))}


EVIDENCE_FIRST = {  # profile trait / goal -> evidence kinds to put first
    "not_tracking_costs": ["index"],
    "open_book": ["should_cost"],
    "quality_first": ["quality", "scorecard"],
}


@dataclass
class Plan:
    supplier_id: str
    name: str
    policy: Policy
    profile: SupplierProfile
    open_c: float
    target_c: float
    floor_price: float | None
    full_cost: float | None
    gt: GroundTruth | None = None
    belief: FloorBelief | None = None  # where this supplier will stop with us - recomputed after every reply
    lower_c: float = -math.inf  # C at the supplier's estimated floor: take it at once
    upper_c: float = math.inf  # the most we accept when the deal is at risk - never said, never asked for
    evidence: list[Evidence] = field(default_factory=list)
    banned_kinds: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
    our_c: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)  # the C we asked for, per round
    last_claims: list[Evidence] = field(default_factory=list)
    seen_replies: int = 0
    stalls: int = 0
    probed_final: bool = False
    price_matched: bool = False
    requests: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)  # levers the supplier asked for in its e-mails
    last_keys: frozenset = frozenset()  # the structures and prices we sent last
    offered: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # structure -> the highest price we offered for it
    volume_proved: bool = False
    proposed: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # field -> values the supplier put on its own sheets
    text_price: float | None = None  # a lower price it wrote in the text but not on a sheet
    text_price_used: bool = False
    alternatives_taken: set = field(default_factory=set)
    counters: list = field(default_factory=list)  # facts from its own e-mails that answer it - spent first
    used_sentences: set = field(default_factory=set)
    lever_turn: bool = False  # this round our step goes into a structure we have not offered yet
    pressures: list = field(default_factory=list)  # cost drivers it says weigh on it
    request_counts: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # lever -> replies that asked for it
    reanchored: bool = False
    asked_breakdown: bool = False
    breakdown_read: bool = False


# Candidate changes from the reviews, each switchable so it can be measured on its own (simulator with
# --jitter --strangers, then the sandbox) before it is adopted. Off by default.
FLAGS = {
    "strict_final": "a final offer: only its cheaper alternative, accept, or the RFQ probe - no written-price ask",
    "belief_cap": "the belief's extrapolation: step ratio capped at 0.6, never under 90 % of its lowest offer value",
    "probe_leader": "RFQ probe only when our ask is below the best offer on the table",
    "anchor_cap25": "first ask at most 25 % under the quote in total (base depth plus the data's extra)",
    "dedupe_series": "one argument per index series and case",
    "big_steps": "from round 2 our step is 2-4 % of C_open (at most 60 % of the gap)",
}


class TacticalStrategy(BaselineStrategy):
    name = "tactical"

    def __init__(self, data: WorldData | None = None, llm=None, **flags) -> None:
        super().__init__(data, llm)
        unknown = set(flags) - set(FLAGS)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown tactical flags: {sorted(unknown)}")
        self.flags = {name: bool(flags.get(name, False)) for name in FLAGS}
        self.used_series: set[str] = set()
        self.tplans: dict[str, Plan] = {}
        self.banned_case_kinds: set[str] = set()  # contradicted: never again in this case

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ prepare
    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None:
        buyer = neg.buyer
        goal = buyer.get("category_goal", "routine")
        parts = neg.case.get("parts", [])
        current = buyer.get("current_unit_price")
        for sid, thread in neg.threads.items():
            _, terms = thread.standing
            profile = build_profile(self.data, sid, neg.case)
            policy = self._policy(goal, profile)
            full_cost = self._full_cost(parts, sid)
            self._estimate_supplier(neg, sid, full_cost, profile)
            floor = self._floor(neg, full_cost, policy)
            open_c = neg.cost(sid, terms)
            gt = estimate(self.data, neg.case, sid, terms.get("unit_price"), tuple(profile.traits))
            if gt.lower and goal not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
                floor = gt.lower  # one floor: the ground truth's (it knows below-cost sellers and countries)
            target_c = self._target_c(neg, sid, terms, policy, profile, floor, current, gt)
            plan = Plan(sid, self._name(sid), policy, profile, open_c, target_c, floor, full_cost, gt)
            plan.lower_c, plan.upper_c = self._bounds_c(neg, sid, terms, gt, target_c, open_c)
            if terms.get("unit_price") is not None:
                rate = buyer.get("interest_rate", 0.08) * (2 if profile.has("cash_short") else 1)
                plan.belief = FloorBelief(neg.case, terms, thread.standard_terms, gt.lower, rate)
                plan.belief.capped = self.flags["belief_cap"]
                plan.belief.ppm = profile.ppm  # scorecard ppm: what a chargeback really costs it
            plan.evidence = self._evidence(neg, sid, terms.get("unit_price"), current) if terms else []
            if profile.has("hedged"):
                plan.banned_kinds.add("index")  # "not our reality" until its hedge runs out
            if gt.market_supports_ask:
                plan.banned_kinds.add("index")  # the indices back its ask: citing them helps it, not us
            self.tplans[sid] = plan
            neg.recorder.event(
                "plan",
                session_id=neg.session_id,
                case_id=neg.case_id,
                supplier_id=sid,
                strategy=self.name,
                goal=goal,
                policy=policy.__dict__,
                profile=profile.summary(),
                trait_refs=profile.traits,
                open_price=terms.get("unit_price"),
                open_c=open_c,
                target_c=target_c,
                lower_c=plan.lower_c,
                upper_c=plan.upper_c,
                ground_truth=gt.summary(),
                c_alt=neg.c_alt,
                floor_price=floor,
                full_cost=full_cost,
                evidence=[{"kind": e.kind, "refs": e.refs, "sentence": e.sentence} for e in plan.evidence],
            )
            log.info(
                "%s plan [%s %s]: price open %s lower %s upper %s (asked %s%%, justified %s%%) | C target %s upper %s",
                sid,
                goal,
                ",".join(sorted(profile.traits)) or "-",
                terms.get("unit_price"),
                gt.lower,
                gt.upper,
                gt.asked_pct,
                gt.justified_pct,
                _k(target_c),
                _k(plan.upper_c),
            )

    def _policy(self, goal: str, p: SupplierProfile) -> Policy:
        base = POLICIES.get(goal, DEFAULT_POLICY)
        anchor, beta, recip = base.anchor, base.beta, base.reciprocity
        trade = list(base.trade_first)
        if p.has("underutilised"):
            anchor, beta = anchor + 0.03, beta + 0.5
        markup = base.markup
        if p.has("full_order_book") or p.has("below_cost"):
            anchor = max(0.02, anchor - 0.03)
            markup = max(markup, 0.0)  # no room under its cost: it is already there or does not need us
        if p.has("price_frozen"):
            anchor = max(0.02, anchor - 0.02)
        if p.has("approval_ladder"):
            beta += 0.5  # it moves in small approved steps: no reason for us to move fast
        if p.has("cash_short"):
            trade.insert(0, "payment_days")
        if p.has("wants_volume") or p.has("full_order_book") or p.has("price_frozen"):
            trade += ["contract_months", "volume_per_year"]
        if p.has("we_pay_late") or p.has("relationship"):
            recip = min(1.0, recip + 0.1)
        return Policy(anchor, beta, recip, markup, base.claims_first, tuple(dict.fromkeys(trade)))

    def _evidence(self, neg, sid, open_price, current):
        out = super()._evidence(neg, sid, open_price, current)
        if self.data:
            out += self.data.evidence_orders(neg.case.get("parts", []), sid, open_price)
            out += data_facts(self.data, neg.case.get("parts", []))
        return sorted(out, key=lambda e: -e.strength)

    def _full_cost(self, parts: list[str], supplier_id: str) -> float | None:
        """The should-cost of THIS supplier's plant for a single-part case; None otherwise.

        Another supplier's estimate is a different plant (cost base, process) and a bundle's price is
        not one part's cost: guessing would push the floor and the margin charge the wrong way."""
        if not self.data or len(parts) != 1:
            return None
        rows = self.data.query(
            "SELECT unit_cost FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ? AND supplier_id = ? ORDER BY estimate_date DESC",
            (parts[0], supplier_id),
        )
        return rows[0]["unit_cost"] if rows and rows[0]["unit_cost"] else None

    def _estimate_supplier(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, full_cost: float | None, p: SupplierProfile) -> None:
        """Our estimate of the supplier for the relationship term in C (stabilise, secure_supply)."""
        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") not in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS or not full_cost:
            neg.supplier_estimates.pop(sid, None)
            return
        std = neg.threads[sid].standard_terms
        if not {"payment_days", "incoterm"} <= std.keys():
            # no estimate without its standard terms: filling them in made the charge dominate every move (P01/P02
            # stopped negotiating in a dry run) - the shallow strategic anchor guards against the squeeze instead
            return
        rate = neg.buyer.get("interest_rate", 0.08)
        neg.supplier_estimates[sid] = {
            "full_cost": full_cost,
            "interest_rate": rate * 2 if p.has("cash_short") else rate,  # money now is dearer to it
            "usual_rate": rate,
            "standard": std,
        }

    def _update_upper(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str, plan: Plan) -> None:
        """The upper bound follows the evidence: where this supplier will stop with us (its offers, last words,
        the shrinking path of its steps), priced on the best structure. Offline on 28 practice sessions this
        estimate met the real stopping point within 8 % before the first reply and 1-3 % by round 3-4.
        The anchor stays where the data put it; only how far we go and when we take it follow the supplier."""
        _, theirs = neg.threads[sid].standing
        insisted = {r for r, n in plan.request_counts.items() if n >= 2}
        stop_c, stop_terms = plan.belief.best_package(
            lambda t: neg.cost(sid, t),
            lambda t: neg.keeps_must_haves(sid, t),
            allow=lambda t: all(satisfies(neg.case, t, theirs or {}, r, plan.proposed) for r in insisted),
        )
        if not math.isfinite(stop_c):
            return
        _, terms = neg.threads[sid].standing
        cap = min(neg.c_alt, neg.cost(sid, terms) if terms else math.inf, plan.open_c)
        before = plan.upper_c
        plan.upper_c = min(max(stop_c * (1 + STOP_MARGIN), plan.target_c * (1 + UPPER_ROOM)), cap)
        neg.recorder.event(
            "belief",
            session_id=neg.session_id,
            supplier_id=sid,
            belief=plan.belief.summary(),
            stop_c=round(stop_c, 2),
            stop_price=(stop_terms or {}).get("unit_price"),
            upper_before=round(before, 2) if math.isfinite(before) else None,
            upper_after=round(plan.upper_c, 2) if math.isfinite(plan.upper_c) else None,
        )
        log.info(
            "%s belief: stop ~%s (price %s), upper %s -> %s",
            sid,
            _k(stop_c),
            (stop_terms or {}).get("unit_price"),
            _k(before),
            _k(plan.upper_c),
        )

    def _floor(self, neg: Negotiation, full_cost: float | None, policy: Policy) -> float | None:
        if not full_cost:
            return None
        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            margin = neg.buyer.get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
            return round(full_cost / (1 - margin / 100), 2)
        return round(full_cost * (1 + policy.markup), 2)

    def _target_c(self, neg, sid, terms, policy, profile, floor, current, gt: GroundTruth | None = None) -> float:
        """The C of our first ask: the deepest credible price on our C-optimal terms - just under the
        supplier's estimated floor when we have one, else an anchor below the reference price."""
        open_price = terms.get("unit_price")
        if open_price is None:
            return math.inf
        price_only = bool(gt and gt.lower and gt.lower >= open_price * 0.95)  # the prior says: only the price moves
        depth = ANCHOR_PRICE_ONLY if price_only else ANCHOR_WITH_LEVERS
        extra = ANCHOR_DATA_EXTRA
        if neg.buyer.get("category_goal") in RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            depth, extra = min(depth, ANCHOR_RELATIONSHIP), 0.0  # squeezing a strategic supplier costs us C
        # round 1 carries 67 % of all supplier movement and no supplier ever walked over a deep first offer
        # (0 of 917 replies); within a case deeper first offers went with better scores - so we open deep
        candidates = [open_price * (1 - depth)]
        if gt and gt.lower and gt.grounded:
            candidates.append(gt.lower * (1 - UNDER_FLOOR))
        alt_price = ((neg.buyer.get("alternative") or {}).get("terms") or {}).get("unit_price")
        if alt_price and alt_price < open_price:
            candidates.append(alt_price * 0.98)
        # the data may take it deeper - a cheaper alternative, a low grounded floor - but not past 5 points more
        if self.flags["anchor_cap25"]:
            extra = max(0.0, min(extra, 0.25 - depth))
        price = max(min(candidates), open_price * (1 - depth - extra))
        # no hard floor for strategic suppliers: the relationship term already prices a squeeze in C, and
        # our cost estimate can sit above its real one (P02: should-cost 380 over a 371 quote, C_best ~364)
        price = min(price, open_price)
        ideal = complete_offer(neg.case, self._optimise(neg, sid, {**terms, "unit_price": round(price, 2)}))
        return min(neg.cost(sid, ideal), neg.cost(sid, terms))

    def _bounds_c(self, neg, sid, terms, gt: GroundTruth, target_c: float, open_c: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """The bounds in C, on our C-optimal terms: a fair price on poor terms (a short contract that
        leaves need uncovered, early payment, dear freight) must not pass as a good deal."""
        lower_c, upper_c = -math.inf, min(open_c, neg.c_alt)
        if gt.lower:
            lower_c = neg.cost(sid, self._ideal(neg, sid, terms, gt.lower))
        if gt.upper:
            upper_c = min(upper_c, neg.cost(sid, self._ideal(neg, sid, terms, gt.upper)))
        # room to concede above our first ask, whatever the calibration says (P05: an 18 % anchor over a 22 %
        # floor left upper == anchor and only 0.4 % steps) - never above its quote or our alternative
        return lower_c, min(max(upper_c, target_c * (1 + UPPER_ROOM)), open_c, neg.c_alt)

    def _ideal(self, neg, sid, terms: dict, price: float) -> dict:
        return complete_offer(neg.case, self._optimise(neg, sid, {**terms, "unit_price": round(price, 2)}))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ per thread
    def decide(self, neg: Negotiation, supplier_id: str) -> Decision:
        t, plan = neg.threads[supplier_id], self.tplans[supplier_id]
        if not t.live:
            return Decision.drop(supplier_id, f"thread {t.status}")
        self._learn(neg, supplier_id, plan)
        sheet_id, theirs = neg.best_offer(supplier_id)  # judge it by its best sheet for us, not its first
        if theirs.get("unit_price") is None or not math.isfinite(plan.target_c):
            return Decision.hold(supplier_id, "no price to negotiate on")
        early_signals = reply_signals(t.latest.get("body", ""))
        last_word_now = t.status == "final_offer" or (early_signals["firm"] and t.rounds_used > 0)
        if not (self.flags["strict_final"] and last_word_now):
            if text := self._text_price_offer(neg, supplier_id, plan):
                return text  # it wrote a lower price than it sheeted: ask for that first
        if t.status == "agreed":
            if take := self._take_agreed(neg, supplier_id):
                return take

"""The middle layer: the kit's `arena-sim` with suppliers fitted from our recorded arena sessions.

Same API as the arena (the kit's simulator underneath), the cases we have played, the arena's own `c_open` and
`c_best` for each as the yardstick, and per supplier a `supplier.Thread` instead of the kit's fixed script. It
costs no practice session and no token: use it to rank strategy changes before a practice run confirms them.

    negotiator sim calibrate          fit the suppliers from runs/ -> data/sim/model.json
    negotiator sim check              how well the fit predicts sessions it has not seen
    negotiator sim bench a b c        play strategies on the simulator, next to their arena scores
    negotiator sim serve              the simulator as a local arena, for `negotiator --url ...`

What it cannot tell you: anything about wording. The simulated supplier reads term sheets and cited IDs, not
the e-mail, so tone, questions, unbacked claims and leaks have no effect here - on the arena they do.
"""

import logging
import random
import socket
import statistics
import threading
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

import arena_kit.sim as kit
from arena_kit.cost import closing_terms, cost_breakdown, must_haves_ok, score, total_cost

from negotiator.sim.calibrate import _moves, as_objects, best_cost, calibrate, estimate
from negotiator.sim.pricing import value_of
from negotiator.sim.supplier import PERSONAS, Profile, Thread

CLAIM_TYPES = {
    "idx": "index_change",
    "quote": "rival_quote",
    "offer": "rival_quote",
    "sc": "delivery_record",
    "qn": "quality_record",
    "cost": "should_cost",
    "doc": "notice_period",
    "ctr": "notice_period",
    "po": "order_prices",
    "fc": "forecast",
    "news": "news",
}
MAX_CLAIMS = 3
SIM_URL, SIM_KEY = "http://127.0.0.1:8100", "sim"  # where `sim serve` listens, and the key it always accepts


def price_cap(case: dict, ref: dict, c_best: float):
    """structure -> the unit price at which it costs the buyer exactly c_best (C is linear in the price)."""

    def cap(structure: dict) -> float:
        c1 = total_cost(case, {**structure, "unit_price": 1.0}, ref)
        c2 = total_cost(case, {**structure, "unit_price": 2.0}, ref)
        return 1.0 + (c_best - c1) / (c2 - c1) if c2 > c1 else 0.0

    return cap


JITTER = 0.3  # with --jitter a floor moves by up to this share of the supplier's room, either way


def session_profiles(model: dict, case: dict, rng: random.Random, strangers: bool, jitter: bool) -> tuple[dict, float]:
    """The suppliers of one session and the c_best that goes with them. Unchanged, that is the arena's own figure;
    with moved floors it moves by as much as the model's best package does."""
    known = model["results"][case["case_id"]]
    profiles = {sup: model["profiles"][f"{case['case_id']}|{sup}"] for sup in case["suppliers"]}
    before = min(best_cost(case, p) for p in profiles.values()) if jitter else 0.0
    for sup, p in list(profiles.items()):
        changes = {}
        if strangers:  # the same economics, the habits of another supplier
            d = model["profiles"][rng.choice(sorted(model["profiles"]))]
            changes.update(steps=d.steps, finals=d.finals, convinced=d.convinced)
        if jitter:
            changes["floor"] = p.floor + rng.uniform(-JITTER, JITTER) * (p.opening_value - p.floor)
        if changes:
            profiles[sup] = Profile(**{**p.__dict__, **changes})
    c_best = known["c_best"]
    if jitter:
        c_best += min(best_cost(case, p) for p in profiles.values()) - before
        c_best = min(c_best, known["c_open"] - 0.02 * abs(known["c_open"]))  # there is always room to negotiate
    return profiles, c_best


def new_thread(model: dict, case: dict, sup: str, rng: random.Random, profile: Profile | None = None,
               c_best: float | None = None, persona: str = "fitted") -> Thread:  # fmt: skip
    profile = profile or model["profiles"][f"{case['case_id']}|{sup}"]
    c_best = model["results"][case["case_id"]]["c_best"] if c_best is None else c_best
    return Thread(profile, model["pool"], rng, cap=price_cap(case, profile.ref, c_best), persona=PERSONAS[persona])


def _text(value):
    if isinstance(value, dict):  # an index clause, as the arena's quote PDF writes it
        return (
            f"{value['series']}, {round(value['material_share'] * 100)}% material, "
            f"deadband {float(value['deadband_pct'])} %, base {value.get('base_month')}"
        )
    return value


class CalibratedSim(kit.Sim):
    """The kit's simulator with fitted suppliers, the arena's yardstick and no practice quota."""

    def __init__(self, model: dict, facts=None, seed: int = 0, strangers: bool = False, no_clock: bool = True,
                 persona: str = "fitted", jitter: bool = False):  # fmt: skip
        super().__init__(model["cases"], facts, no_clock=no_clock)
        self.model, self.seed, self.strangers, self.persona, self.jitter = model, seed, strangers, persona, jitter
        self.opened = defaultdict(int)

    def practice(self, team):
        return {"used": 0, "left": kit.PRACTICE_LIMIT, "limit": kit.PRACTICE_LIMIT, "resets_at": None}

    def open(self, team, case_id):
        case = self.cases.get(case_id)
        if case is None:
            raise kit.Fail(404, "no such case")
        if sum(s["status"] == "open" for s in self._mine(team)) >= kit.MAX_OPEN:
            raise kit.Fail(429, f"at most {kit.MAX_OPEN} open sessions per key")
        sid = f"sim{next(self.ids)}"
        self.opened[case_id] += 1
        s = {"id": sid, "team": team, "case": case, "status": "open", "end_reason": None, "threads": {},
             "files": {}, "offers": {}, "used": set(), "result": None, "trace": [], "moves": [],
             "created_at": self.clock(), "late": set()}  # fmt: skip
        fixed = case.get("fixed_terms", {})
        world = random.Random(f"{self.seed}/{case_id}/{self.opened[case_id]}")
        profiles, s["c_best"] = session_profiles(self.model, case, world, self.strangers, self.jitter)
        for sup in case["suppliers"]:
            rng = random.Random(f"{self.seed}/{case_id}/{self.opened[case_id]}/{sup}")
            sim = new_thread(self.model, case, sup, rng, profiles[sup], s["c_best"], self.persona)
            p = sim.profile
            standard = {k: v for k, v in p.ref.items() if k not in fixed and k != "unit_price"}
            th = s["threads"][sup] = {"key": sup.split(":", 1)[1], "round": 0, "n": 0, "timeouts": 0,
                                      "closed": None, "last_at": self.clock(), "messages": [], "late": [],
                                      "standard": standard, "opening": p.opening_value, "sim": sim}  # fmt: skip
            self._mail(s, th, "open", dict(p.opening), "Our quote is attached.", ["quote.pdf"])
            s["trace"].append({"round": 0, "actor": sup, "move": kit.structured(th["messages"][0], 0), "reasons": []})
        self.sessions[sid] = s
        return {
            "session_id": sid,
            "case": case,
